texts: The Weight of Ash Elara digs through the gray silt covering her cellar door. She finds her brother Elias's locket buried in the muck, crushed into the floorboards. The ash consumes metal and wood alike. Elias did not leave; he was buried where he stood.

The Ashfall Gate Elias unearths a sealed iron trunk beneath the frozen soil of Ashfall. Instead of gold or secrets, the box contains a functioning, humming radio broadcasting his own voice from three days in the future. The Ashfall soil preserves sound. The future is mutable but predictable.
The First Layer Elara scrapes thick gray soot from the window frame. She finds a human tooth embedded in the ash. The ash contains remnants of people. Elara is alone in the house.

The Static Test Elias speaks a specific word into the soil to check the delay. He waits. The radio emits only the sound of a shovel hitting stone, repeating the exact moment he opened the trunk. The radio does not broadcast future events. It broadcasts trapped echoes.

Sarah at the Ridge Sarah watches from the ridge as Elias digs. She sees him pull the iron trunk from the ice and press his ear to the metal lid. She records his movements in a ledger while her own radio hums with the same frequency as the one in the hole. Sarah is monitoring Elias and she possesses a matching device that connects to his.

The Frequency of Soil Elias presses his ear to the trunk. The iron vibrates against his skin. His future voice describes a fire in the supply shed that has not happened yet. The trunk acts as a temporal antenna. Elias recognizes his own tone but not the words.

The Preventative Measure Elias sprints to the supply shed. He dumps a bucket of snow over the pile of kerosene-soaked rags before they ignite. He finds a discarded cigarette butt inside the shed, still smoldering. The future predicted by the radio can be prevented. Someone is watching him.

Matches and Friction Elias strikes a match to see inside the iron trunk. He realizes the metal lining is etched with tally marks that correspond to his own heartbeat. The radio signal shifts from his future voice to the rhythmic sound of dripping water. The trunk reacts to human presence by mirroring internal states.

Mara's Observation Mara watches Elias from behind the collapsed barn. She sees him tremble, eyes fixed on the iron trunk. She knows the trunk is empty. She does not hear the voice Elias hears. Mara believes Elias is hallucinating or lying.

prose Elias drags the match head across the rusted hinge. Sulfur flares blue. He holds the flame over the interior. The steel floor is covered in deep, jagged gouges. Five hundred marks. A thousand. They vibrate in time with the pulse in his neck. The radio emits a wet, hollow slap. Plip. Plip. The sound of water hitting deep stone. The future voice vanishes. The radio speaker bulges and leaks a dark, viscous fluid onto his knuckles.

prose Mara kneels behind the frozen swell of the ridge. She watches Elias. He crouches by the open trunk. The match flame flickers in his hand. It casts long, jagged shadows against the iron walls. Elias stares at the inner lining. He touches a tally mark with his thumb. His chest heaves. The tally marks vibrate in sync with his panicked breaths. A sudden squelch of water erupts from the radio speaker. It echoes off the permafrost. Elias drops the match. The box swallows the light. Mara pulls her coat tight. She knows that sound. She heard it in the vents of the colony before the rot took the pumps.

prose Elias drags a match against the iron lid. The sulfur flare illuminates deep gouges in the metal. He runs a thumb over the scratches. They are precise, rhythmic. His thumb pulses in time with the marks. The radio emits a low pop. The voice cuts out. It is replaced by the wet, rhythmic drip of water hitting stone. Elias presses his palm to the trunk. The iron is cold now, but his pulse thrums against the etching. The tally marks shift under his touch.

The Viscosity of Memory Elias wipes the black fluid from his skin. He examines the stain under his fingernails and realizes it is not oil but thick, brackish pond water teeming with dormant silt. He tastes the salt on his tongue. The trunk interior begins to pulse with light as the fluid flows into the etched tally marks, filling them like capillaries. The dark fluid is not mechanical lubricant, but biological, linked to the tally marks in the box.

Corrosive Contact The viscous fluid burns through Elias's skin. He drops the radio. The device lands face-down and its speaker emits a high-pitched metallic whine that causes the surrounding frozen soil of Ashfall to crack and shift, threatening to collapse the hole he is standing in. The radio's fluid is caustic. The device interacts physically with the environment.

Stained Connection The dark fluid spreads rapidly, soaking into Elias's skin. His skin at the point of contact begins to turn the same gray, metallic shade as the trunk. He tries to pull his hand away, but the radio magnetism locks him in place, forcing him to watch his own veins darken toward his heart. The trunk is parasitic and is actively consuming Elias's physical vitality.

prose Elias swipes his palm against his denim thigh. The black smear stays. He lifts a hand to the moonlight. Fine grains of grey silt sit in the creases of his skin. He drags a fingernail through the muck. It is cold. He touches his tongue to his knuckle. The taste is dead lake. Salt. Rot. Stagnant reeds. The radio hums louder now. A thin line of the fluid snakes toward the nearest gouge in the floor. It hits the steel and snaps into the groove. The mark glows a dull, sickly amber. Another flows. Then a dozen. The light crawls across the bottom of the trunk like a vein filling with blood. The metal floor warms under his knees.

prose Elias rubs his thumb against his palm. The black grit smears. He brings his hand to his nose. It smells of dead reeds and cold lake bottom. He touches his tongue to his skin. Bitter salt stings his throat. He spits onto the frozen dirt. Inside the trunk, the fluid creeps along the jagged steel scars. The marks glow white. A faint, low hum rattles his teeth. Elias grips the edge of the trunk. He tries to push the lid shut, but the metal holds fast. The light pulses faster. He stares at the tally marks. They look like veins pumping beneath the steel.

prose Mara watches from the tree line. The flashlight beam cuts a sharp wedge through the fog. She sees Elias kneel. His hands shake. He smears the black sludge against his denim coat. It is not grease. It is stagnant water from the basin. The silt moves under the trunk light. It flows into the metal grooves like blood in a vein. The tally marks glow. They are not scratches anymore. They are maps.

The Ignition Sequence The warming floor intensifies, scorching the denim against Elias's knees. He reaches to pull the radio, but the trunk locks tight, snapping a steel shutter over the speaker to trap his fingers. Outside, the scent of smoke curls through the doorway; the supply shed fire his future voice predicted has begun, but it is moving toward him now. The trunk controls Elias's environment, and the future warning is becoming a present threat.

The Circuit of Salt The amber light hits the final tally mark. The trunk floor collapses into a deep, vertical shaft. Elias drops his flashlight into the hole, but it strikes a surface only inches below the iron frame. He looks down to see a reflection of his own face looking up from a layer of dark, stagnant water trapped within the iron casing. The tally marks act as a circuit lock; the trunk is a container for water that contains a memory or a physical manifestation of Elias.

The Price of Transmission The amber light from the tally marks surges, burning Elias's fingertips where he touches the rim. The radio broadcasts his own scream before he makes a sound, and his skin begins to bruise in the exact pattern of the glowing gouges. He tries to pull his hands away, but the metal floor adheres to his palms like heated wax. He realizes the tally marks are not count records, but slots for human blood. The trunk requires physical sacrifice to function and feeds on Elias's vitality to fuel its transmissions.

The Steel Shutter The trunk floor glows white-hot, burning through Elias's jeans. He tries to jerk his hand back, but the radio’s speaker frame collapses into a rigid steel mouth. It clamps onto his fingers, grinding bone against the metal tally marks. The radio emits a high-pitched, harmonic whine that drowns out the distant roar of the shed fire. The trunk is a trap that uses physical pain to finalize its process.

The Sentry's Vantage Kael watches from the supply shed doorway. He sees Elias kneeling at the trunk, unaware of the smoldering fuse trailing from the shed floor toward the container. Kael notices the trunk's metal lid shifting, not by Elias's hand, but as if the box itself is hunting him. Kael knows about the trunk and the encroaching fire before Elias.

The Heat Exchange Elias hammers the radio with his free fist to break the steel shutter. Each impact forces the radio to broadcast his own screams from the near future, perfectly synced to his own throat. As the shed walls groan under encroaching flames, the glowing tally marks on the trunk floor surge with heat, branding the skin of his trapped fingers with the exact shape of the notches. The trunk is actively harvesting Elias's physical experiences to power itself.

prose The floor of the trunk turns white. Denim smokes. Elias yanks his arm, but the steel shutter bites down. Bone clicks against metal. The radio frame shifts, metal teeth locking over his knuckles. A high-pitched whine cuts the air. It swallows the sound of the burning shed outside. The dark fluid on his hand surges. It flows into the metal mouth, coating the tally marks in a thick, slick coat. The glow of the marks turns blinding. Elias pulls again. The trunk does not yield. It pulls back.

prose Elias screams. The metal teeth bite to the knuckle bone. Dark fluid wells from the radio, boiling where it touches his skin. The scent of scorched meat fills the small trunk. Outside, the shed roof collapses with a thunderous crack. The firelight paints his knuckles orange. Beneath his trapped fingers, the tally marks flicker from amber to a blinding, lethal white. The radio hums the pitch of a circular saw. Elias pulls. The trunk does not yield. His skin tears, leaving a strip of denim and flesh caught in the iron teeth.

prose The floor of the trunk turns translucent, revealing a mesh of copper wires pulsing beneath the white-hot steel. Elias screams, but the sound dies in the high-pitched whine of the radio. He yanks his arm. The steel mouth bites deeper. Bone clicks against the metal tally marks. They flicker, drinking the dark fluid leaking from his knuckles. He smells singed denim and hair. Outside, the shed fire pops as a support beam collapses. Elias lunges forward with his free hand, gripping the radio frame to pry the shutter open. His skin peels away from the heat. He does not pull back. He wants to know what the radio says next.

The Observer's Insight Inside the trunk, the inner iron lining hums. A small, lidless eye peers from a seam near the radio speaker. It watches Elias suffer. It does not feel empathy. It records the heat levels and the bone density of the fingers trapped in the shutter. The eye blinks, a wet, mechanical motion. It confirms the process has reached the required threshold of agony. The trunk is a sentient or semi-sentient observer that requires pain for its operation.

The Price of Transmission The dark fluid pulses through Elias's crushed knuckles, siphoning life. His arm grows cold as the radio begins to hum his childhood nickname in his own voice. The tally marks shift from amber to a blinding, rhythmic red, matching his frantic heartbeat. A sharp, needle-like protrusion rises from the radio's speaker to pierce his thumb. The radio feeds on Elias's blood. It possesses deep, intimate knowledge of his history.

The Feedback Loop The high-pitched whine from the radio reaches a frequency that vibrates the trunk floor, causing the iron casing to liquefy. As the metal turns into a molten slurry, the tally marks overflow and pull Elias's fingers deeper into the radio's interior, merging his flesh with the circuitry. The radio starts broadcasting his own screams from the near future, creating a feedback loop that shakes the supply shed walls. The radio is consuming biological matter to finalize its broadcast; the trunk is not just a container, but an organic-mechanical interface.

The Extraction Elias stops fighting the trunk. He presses his other hand against the iron floor, seeking the heat. The radio pulse syncs with his heartbeat. The steel shutter relaxes, then snaps shut, severing the tip of his ring finger. The trunk swallows the digit, dragging it into a glowing slot. The trunk requires biological sacrifice to process its contents.

The Price of Completion As the tally marks glow white, the trunk pulls backward with rhythmic force, snapping a bone in Elias's wrist. The radio falls silent. The dark fluid stops flowing. A single, final tally mark carves itself into the iron beside Elias's thumb. The trunk lid slams open, dropping Elias onto the cold floor of the shed. The tally marks act as a counter for the trunk's power-up cycle; reaching the end of the count triggers the trunk's release mechanism.

The Structural Failure The shed floor groans under the weight of the encroaching fire. A support beam snaps. The vibration travels through the frozen soil and hits the trunk. The iron casing buckles, jamming the locking mechanism mid-cycle. The shutter freezes halfway, pinning Elias’s fingers at an awkward, agonizing angle against a jagged, unfinished tally mark. He cannot pull away, and the trunk refuses to release. The trunk is not a closed loop; it is susceptible to the environment.

prose Elias stills his breathing. He stops the tug of war. The iron floor burns through his skin, a steady, rhythmic heat. It beats against his palm. Thump. Thump. The radio matches the pace. The steel shutter plate shudders, sliding back an inch. Elias does not pull. He presses his left hand into the hot metal. His right hand stays caught. Metal teeth bite. The snap is clean. A hot, sharp pinch at the knuckle. Elias watches the ring finger tip fall. It does not hit the floor. A slot opens in the base of the trunk. It glows a deep, wet red. The trunk drags the finger inside.

prose Elias lets his shoulder drop. He stops pulling. He presses his left palm flat against the iron floor. The surface is a furnace. It pulses. The hum inside his chest aligns with the beat of the metal. Thump. Thump. The shutter releases with a mechanical sigh. Elias jerks back. The hinge snaps shut. A hot spark leaps from the iron. His ring finger ends in a jagged, dark line. The tip is gone. The trunk pulls the severed flesh into a glowing aperture. The light shifts from amber to a wet, raw violet. The radio falls silent. Outside, the fire finds the shed wall.

prose Elias drops his dead weight against the iron rim. He stops the thrashing. He presses his left palm into the floor, matching the heat. The radio pulse hits his palm. It thumps against his palm like a second heart. The steel shutter clicks. It drops. The ring finger snaps off at the knuckle. The trunk floor opens a jagged, glowing slot. It pulls the digit into the dark. Bone scrapes iron. The radio voice stops. The silence is louder than the fire.
